hero.title: Stop running one AI agent at a time.
hero.sub: Opus plans. Cheap and free models execute. A reviewer from another provider checks the diff. Every turn spends the minimum number of tokens.
hero.installNote: One command on macOS, Linux and Windows.
hero.petLabel: The lead agent, our mascot. It cheers when you copy the install command.

why.label: Why
why.title:
One agent at a time
is the bottleneck.
why.caption: Without the stack compared with the stack, row by row
rows: One agent at a time; you are the bottleneck
The lead plans and fans out parallel workers, each in an isolated git worktree
A hook blocks Opus subagents; the default becomes Sonnet; reading goes to Haiku/Gemini
Heavy reading uses Google quota (agy); mechanical edits use free models (NVIDIA via 9Router)
A curator probes models 3×/day and rewrites the combo on its own
Terminal output and context bloat every turn
RTK compresses shell output, caveman trims replies, graphify replaces broad reads
Rules live in CLAUDE.md and get ignored
Rules become enforcement: hooks, kernel sandbox, orchestrator policy
No spec, giant prompts, blind diffs
Spec Kit SDD: specify → clarify → plan → tasks → analyze → implement → review → verify
You only know what happened by opening the laptop
Hermes sends a daily digest + plan of the day to Discord/Telegram

orchestration.label: Orchestration
orchestration.title:
Plan big.
Execute small.
orchestration.intro: Text rules do not work; enforcement does. The lead splits work by type and sends each type to the cheapest executor that still delivers the quality required.

scout.role: Reading and search that needs a shell. Returns a conclusion with file:line, never the whole file.
scout.guard: Allowed: model pinned in the agent definition.

builder.role: Implements planned units, runs the checks, does not commit. Opus only for deep or risky units.
builder.guard: Allowed: model pinned in the agent definition.

reviewer.role: Reads the diff against the acceptance criteria and hunts for bugs without editing.
reviewer.guard: Allowed: model pinned in the agent definition.

agy.role: Heavy read-only scouting with Gemini Flash. With Claude Opus via agy, an independent reviewer.
agy.quota: Google, separate from your Claude subscription
agy.guard: Not a Claude subagent: runs as an alethe worker.

opencode-safe.role: Mechanical edits gated by tests, in an isolated worktree inside a kernel sandbox that denies .env and keys.
opencode-safe.guard: Not a Claude subagent: runs as an alethe worker.

codex.role: Independent bug-hunting review. A different provider is a real second opinion.
codex.guard: Not a Claude subagent: runs as an alethe worker.

lanes.label: Three parallel worktree lanes, and an Opus subagent blocked at the gate

sdd.label: Spec-driven development
sdd.title:
Spec first.
Code second.
sdd.intro: The spec is the contract. Decisions stay with the lead; implement is where delegation pays.

steps.why: user stories and acceptance criteria, in spec.md
always run it: it kills ambiguity before it becomes code
spec, plan and tasks cross-checked before any code
delegated to builders, one worktree each
a reviewer on another provider gets the task and the full diff
tests, typecheck, and a manual run of the real feature

sdd.fanLabel: tasks.md fans out parallel tasks to builders, each in its own worktree

tokens.label: Token economy
tokens.title:
Measured,
not promised.
tokens.intro: Real numbers from the author's machine, straight from rtk gain --monthly (24,431 shell commands run by agents).
tokens.barsLabel: Share of shell output tokens saved, by month, on a 0 to 30 percent scale

rows.month: 2026-11 (stack set up early in the month, partial)

tokens.footnote: That is one developer and one workload, and November is a partial month, so read it as a trend, not a benchmark. Savings from delegation (subagents, alethe) and caveman are not measured here yet. Measure your own after a week or two.

cards.name: RTK
cards.body: A transparent hook rewrites git status into rtk git status and compresses output (git, ls, tests, docker) before the model sees it. Realistic savings are 15-30% of input tokens, not magic.

cards.name: caveman
cards.body: Makes replies short. That cuts output tokens and, because every turn re-reads the history, the context too. Only replies to you: code, commit messages and PR text stay normal.

cards.name: graphify
cards.body: A knowledge graph of the codebase lives in graphify-out/. Ask it first, so there is no blind grep or file dump.
